question: Should OpenClaw publish `pluginSecretRefSetup` as a stable plugin-SDK contract for provider-owned setup CLIs, or should this PR use a narrower owner-approved alternative?
rationale: The branch changes a documented public plugin-SDK subpath; compatibility, naming, and long-term ownership cannot be inferred safely from the implementation alone.

options.title: Approve the narrow SDK contract
options.body: Accept the helper as the supported shared setup-plan API and retain its documented scope and compatibility tests.

options.title: Keep setup construction out of the public SDK
options.body: Rework the sharing boundary so the 1Password and Vault owners do not publish this new external plugin API.

recommendation.title: Approve the narrow SDK contract
recommendation.body: Accept the helper as the supported shared setup-plan API and retain its documented scope and compatibility tests.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent commits show the closest direct involvement with the proposed SecretRef API and 1Password hardening boundary.
